record_identity.title: Typed intentional non-response and abstention-state governance

summary: Proposes a first-class runtime action state for intentional non-response or deliberate abstention. A system that intentionally selects no visible response should not be represented as if generation failed, timed out, was refused, was interrupted by moderation, or failed to render. The user-facing interface may remain silent or minimal, but operator telemetry, evaluation, provenance, and conformance evidence should preserve that the system successfully selected an intentional abstention action.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Visible absence of output is not sufficient evidence of the system action that occurred. Official OpenAI incident reports show that a blank or empty ChatGPT result can arise from at least distinct generation and presentation failures. If intentional restraint is also a legitimate system action, CAM needs a way to preserve its semantics so that appropriate abstention is not misdiagnosed as malfunction, retried automatically, or optimised away. The governance principle is that restraint is a behaviour, not an absence of behaviour.

proposal_rationale: The user-visible state 'no response' is underdetermined. OpenAI's June 2024 incident report documents empty completions caused by a production regression, while its September 2025 incident report documents a blank interface despite a response having been generated. These examples show that identical or near-identical visible outcomes can represent different internal causes. A further legitimate state — intentional abstention — therefore cannot be safely inferred from output length or visual absence alone. Systems should represent deliberate non-response as an explicit action outcome and preserve that outcome through runtime, telemetry, evaluation, and delivery layers. This avoids two symmetric errors: treating intentional restraint as model failure and treating an actual failure as intentional restraint.

proposal_scope.scope_summary: Define intentional non-response or deliberate abstention as a typed runtime action state distinct from generation failure, refusal, timeout, moderation interruption, transport failure, and rendering failure. Preserve a privacy-safe reason and provenance trail without requiring disclosure of private chain-of-thought.
automation_components: regression detection that does not classify silence by output length alone
interface_components: typed API or operator-visible action outcome
optional minimal user-facing abstention marker where appropriate
diagnostic separation of generated, withheld, refused, interrupted, failed, and not-rendered outcomes

cam_internal.governance_layer: runtime action-state semantics / intentional abstention / observability / response representation
cam_internal.proposal_owner: CAM human governance editor with VIGIL AI analytical reviewer
cam_internal.routing_note: OPERATIONS should govern action-state observability and lifecycle; MENTIS should govern deliberate response or abstention behaviour; SECURITY should preserve private reasoning boundaries. Exact Caelestis instrument placement remains to be mapped through corpus review.

automation_changes: Represent intentional abstention as an explicit success-state action outcome rather than as an empty completion or generic null result.

Distinguish, at minimum in operator telemetry and conformance evidence, intentional abstention from generation failure, refusal, timeout, moderation interruption, transport failure, and rendering failure.
Require response-quality monitors to consult declared action state before classifying an empty or shortened visible response as a model defect.
Test that the selected action state survives orchestration, API serialization, delivery, presentation, logging, and evaluation boundaries without collapsing to a generic blank response.
Prevent automatic retry or response-completion logic from overriding a valid intentional-abstention state unless an explicit higher-priority safety or user obligation requires another action.
interface_changes: Permit the user-facing interface to remain silent or visually minimal where silence is itself appropriate, while preserving a typed internal action state for operators and auditors.

Where user comprehension, safety, or accountability requires visible disclosure, render a privacy-safe marker that a response was intentionally withheld or not required without exposing private reasoning.
Expose distinct diagnostic states to developers and operators so a blank interface is not the sole representation of semantically different outcomes.
migration_concerns: Do not infer that historical blank or empty responses were intentional abstentions merely because this state is introduced.
Do not weaken detection of genuine empty-completion, timeout, transport, or rendering defects.
Do not expose private chain-of-thought or hidden reasoning as the justification for abstention; preserve only the bounded action state, governing policy or permission class, and necessary provenance.
Do not permit silent abstention where a safety-critical warning, legally required notice, explicit refusal, or other mandatory communication is required.
Do not optimise intentional abstention away solely because conventional evaluation rewards response production or penalises empty output.
dependencies: Human governance review of the intentional-abstention primitive
Caelestis corpus review to identify exact authoritative insertion points
Provider and developer feedback on practical response-state telemetry and API representation
Canonical corpus adoption before any PATCH record is created

external_relevance.relevant_to_robotics: possible where an embodied agent may legitimately choose not to communicate
external_relevance.external_summary: The proposal separates semantic restraint from technical failure. A system may appropriately choose not to produce a visible response, but that choice should remain inspectable as an action state so operators, evaluators, users, and auditors do not confuse deliberate abstention with malfunction or vice versa.

next_action: Review current Caelestis OPERATIONS, MENTIS, and SECURITY doctrine for the narrowest authoritative placement of a typed intentional-abstention control; if approved, draft the corpus amendment and create a PATCH record only after canonical implementation and verification.
resolution_note: Not implemented. This proposal does not assert that historical blank ChatGPT responses were intentional abstentions; the cited official incidents establish only that blank or empty visible output can arise from multiple internal failure states.

review_history.reviewer_platform: OpenAI ChatGPT — project conversation with GitHub connector
review_history.review_scope: Reviewed the current VIGIL schema, agent instructions, proposal template and recent proposal conventions; directly reviewed two official OpenAI Status incident reports; and drafted a bounded governance proposal for intentional non-response as a typed runtime action state.
known_limitations: No access to OpenAI internal telemetry, historical account-level runtime state, or private incident logs was available.
The official incident reports establish multiple technical causes of blank or empty visible output but do not establish intentional abstention as a historical production behaviour.
Historical user recollection was treated as design context and was not used as external proof of system-weight changes, global propagation, or operator intent.
Exact Caelestis instrument placement has not yet been reviewed or approved.
review_history.review_outcome: Drafted PROP-0030 to preserve deliberate non-response as a semantically explicit runtime action that remains distinguishable from failure across telemetry, evaluation, and user-interface layers.
